examples.en: The agent answers customers' questions kindly.
I replied to the inquiry email within a day.
I will answer the questions calmly in the interview.
I'm busy now, so it's hard to answer.

examples.ko: 고객센터에서 답변해 주는 데 이틀 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took two days for the customer center to reply.

examples.ko: 선생님이 묻는 말에 솔직하게 답변하면 돼요.
examples.en: Just answer honestly whatever the teacher asks.

explain: '대답하다'는 이름을 부르는 소리에도 쓰지만, '답변하다'는 질문, 문의, 인터뷰처럼 정식으로 물어본 것에 답할 때만 써요. 친구가 부르면 '대답해'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: When the teacher calls me, I answer in a loud voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름을 부르는 소리나 일상적인 질문에도 쓸 수 있어서 '답변하다'보다 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works for being called by name or for everyday questions, so it is more casual than 답변하다.

phrases.en: Please answer my question.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정식으로 물어본 일에 답을 부탁할 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request for an answer to a formal question.

phrases.en: I will reply to your inquiry today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손님이나 윗사람에게 공손하게 답할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to reply politely to a customer or a superior.

explain_en: '대답하다' can be used even when someone just calls your name, but '답변하다' is only for answering a real question, inquiry, or interview. If a friend calls you, '대답해' is the natural word.

examples.en: This class is run in a question-and-answer format.
I find question-and-answer explanations easy to understand.
This book is in Q&A form, so it is easy to read.
The reporter wrote an interview article in Q&A form.

examples.ko: 면접이 문답식이 아니라 대화처럼 편하게 진행됐어요.
examples.en: The interview was not a strict Q&A but went comfortably like a conversation.
I memorized words by doing a Q&A-style quiz.

explain: 질문과 대답을 주고받는 방식이라는 뜻으로, 주로 '문답식 수업', '문답식 인터뷰'처럼 방식을 말할 때 붙여 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '질문과 대답'이라고 풀어 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: A question-and-answer interview was printed in the magazine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 질문과 대답이 차례로 나오는 인터뷰에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for interviews with questions and answers in turn.

phrases.en: It's a Q&A-style lecture, so it isn't boring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학생과 선생님이 묻고 답하는 수업을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a class where students and teacher ask and answer.

phrases.en: We do a lot of questions and answers in class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 이렇게 풀어 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday talk, people spell it out like this.

explain_en: It describes a format of going back and forth with questions and answers, usually attached to nouns as in '문답식 수업' or '문답식 인터뷰'. In casual talk people may simply say '질문과 대답'.

examples.en: He trailed off, mumbling.
Don't answer vaguely; say it clearly.

examples.ko: 아침부터 어물어물 시간을 보내다 보니 벌써 점심이에요.
examples.en: I dawdled around since morning and now it's already lunchtime.
The child mumbled something vague and went into the room.
Don't try to slip out of it with a vague answer.

examples.ko: 할 말을 못 하고 어물어물 서 있기만 했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't say what I wanted and just stood there fumbling.

explain: 말을 분명히 못 하고 얼버무리거나, 행동이 굼뜬 모습에 써요. '얼버무리다', '넘어가다', '대답하다'와 자주 함께 나와요.

phrases.en: He always mumbles and hesitates when he is asked a question.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어물어물'에 '하다'를 붙여 말이나 행동이 분명하지 않은 모습을 동사로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 하다 makes it a verb for speaking or acting in an unclear, hesitant way.

phrases.en: Don't just gloss over it; tell me honestly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불편한 일을 분명히 말하지 않고 슬쩍 지나갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone slips past an awkward matter without speaking clearly.

phrases.en: He answered vaguely and left.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대답을 분명히 못 하고 얼버무릴 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for giving an unclear, evasive answer.

explain_en: It describes mumbling without saying things clearly, or acting slowly. It often appears with verbs like '얼버무리다', '넘어가다' and '대답하다'.

en: to take action; to take steps

examples.en: If a problem comes up, please deal with it right away.
They say the company has already taken action.
I discussed with the team how to handle it.
If we do not act quickly, there will be big trouble.
It took less than a day to deal with it.
I will send you by email what we did about it.

explain: '조치'는 문제가 생겼을 때 해결하려고 하는 행동이에요. '조치하다'도 쓰지만 '필요한 조치를 취하다'처럼 '조치를 취하다'가 더 자주 들려요. 회사 공지나 고객센터 답변에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: A problem came up, so we quickly took action.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조치하다'보다 더 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This pairing is more common than '조치하다'.

phrases.en: I will take care of it right after I check.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고객에게 해결해 주겠다고 정중하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to politely promise a customer that you will resolve something.
phrases.en_equiv: I will take care of it

phrases.en: I will tell you the result of the action by text message.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해결하려고 한 일의 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for the outcome of the steps taken to solve something.

explain_en: '조치' is an action taken to solve a problem. '조치하다' is used, but '조치를 취하다', as in '필요한 조치를 취하다', is heard more often. You often see it in company notices and customer-service replies.

en: to ask a question; to make an inquiry

examples.ko: 발표가 끝나면 청중이 연사에게 질의할 수 있어요.
examples.en: After the presentation, the audience can ask the speaker questions.
The lawmaker questioned the minister about the policy.
Please send any questions you have by email.

examples.ko: 회의 마지막에 담당자에게 질의하는 시간이 있어요.
examples.en: There is time at the end of the meeting to ask the person in charge questions.

examples.ko: 교수님께 질의하기 전에 질문을 미리 정리해 두세요.
examples.en: Organize your questions in advance before you put them to the professor.

examples.ko: 시청에 전화해서 신청 방법을 질의하려고 해요.
examples.en: I am going to call city hall and ask how to apply.

explain: '질문하다'보다 딱딱해서 국회, 회의, 발표, 공식 문의처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 써요. 친구나 가족에게는 '물어보다'를 써요. '질의응답'은 함께 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.

phrases.en: There is a Q&A session after the presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 묻고 답하는 시간을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for a question-and-answer time.

phrases.en: The minister answered the lawmakers' questions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 질의를 받는 쪽의 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes what the person being questioned does.

phrases.en: May I ask a question during the presentation?
phrases.nuance_ko: 덜 딱딱하고 일상에서도 두루 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less stiff and widely used in daily life.

explain_en: It is stiffer than '질문하다' and is used in formal settings like the National Assembly, meetings, presentations and official inquiries. With friends or family, use '물어보다'. '질의응답' (Q&A) is a common partner word.

examples.en: I listen to the news on the radio every morning.
A session to hear citizens' opinions will be held.
At the meeting, we heard out the employees' complaints.

examples.ko: 음악을 청취하며 공부하면 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: If I study while listening to music, I cannot concentrate.
People who listened to the broadcast sent in their stories.
Tomorrow we will hear the expert's explanation.

explain: '듣다'보다 격식 있는 말이라서 방송, 회의, 공청회에서 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '듣다'를 쓰면 돼요. 기관이나 윗사람이 '의견을 청취하다'처럼 사람들의 말을 들을 때 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I listen to the radio every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '청취하다'와 뜻은 같지만 일상에서 더 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but more natural in everyday speech.

phrases.en: The city hall listened to the residents' opinions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기관이 사람들의 말을 공식적으로 들을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an institution formally hears people's views.

phrases.en: I listen to the news broadcast on my way to work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방송을 듣는다는 뜻으로 격식 있게 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal phrase for listening to a broadcast.

explain_en: It is more formal than '듣다' and is used for broadcasts, meetings, and public hearings. In daily conversation just use '듣다'. Organizations and officials often use it, as in '의견을 청취하다'.

dis.h: formal verb, for broadcasts or hearings
gh: everyday verb for listening or hearing

p.n: Same meaning; 듣다 is plain and everyday.

en: to listen attentively; to listen courteously; to be all ears

examples.ko: 상대방의 말을 끝까지 경청하는 것이 중요해요.
examples.en: It is important to listen attentively to the other person until the end.
The interviewer was listening carefully to the applicant's story.

examples.ko: 선생님 말씀을 경청하면 시험 준비가 쉬워져요.
examples.en: If you listen closely to your teacher, exam prep gets easier.

examples.ko: 친구의 고민을 경청해 줬더니 마음이 편해졌대요.
examples.en: I listened carefully to my friend's worries and he said he felt relieved.
The audience quietly listened to the speaker.

examples.ko: 다른 사람의 의견도 경청할 줄 알아야 해요.
examples.en: You need to know how to listen to other people's opinions too.

explain: '듣다'보다 훨씬 집중해서 존중하는 마음으로 듣는다는 느낌이에요. 회의, 면접, 강연, 상담처럼 조금 격식 있는 자리에서 쓰고, 친구끼리는 '귀 기울여 듣다'라고도 해요. 보통 '말, 의견, 이야기'를 목적어로 써요.

phrases.en: I listened closely to my friend's story.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구 사이에서 '경청하다' 대신 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: What friends often say instead of 'gyeongcheonghada'.

phrases.en: I listened to the customer all the way through.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중간에 끊지 않고 끝까지 듣는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means listening without interrupting until the end.

phrases.en: Everyone, please listen carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의나 강연에서 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking in meetings or lectures.

explain_en: It feels like listening with much more focus and respect than '듣다'. It is used in somewhat formal settings such as meetings, interviews, lectures and counseling, while friends may say '귀 기울여 듣다'. The object is usually 말, 의견 or 이야기.

examples.en: The child began to read the book haltingly.
He explained his situation haltingly.
I asked for directions in halting Korean.
Grandfather told an old story in a faltering voice.
I was so startled that I ended up answering stammeringly.
It's fine to speak haltingly, so take your time.

explain: 말하거나 읽을 때 자꾸 끊기고 서툴게 이어지는 모습을 나타내요. '말했다', '읽었다', '대답했다' 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. '더듬더듬'은 비슷하지만 손으로 더듬어 찾는 모습에도 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I answered the question haltingly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당황해서 대답이 매끄럽지 않을 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits when someone is flustered and the answer doesn't flow.

phrases.en: I read the letters I just learned, slowly and haltingly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서툴러서 읽다가 자꾸 멈출 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when reading is clumsy and keeps stopping.

phrases.en: He went on with his story haltingly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 '더듬더듬'은 손으로 찾는 모습에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, but '더듬더듬' is also used for feeling around by hand.

explain_en: It describes speech or reading that keeps breaking off and proceeds clumsily. It goes well with verbs like '말했다', '읽었다' and '대답했다'. '더듬더듬' is similar but is also used for feeling around with your hands.

examples.en: The US president visits Korea next week.
The famous singer came to Korea to meet fans.
The number of tourists visiting Korea this fall is increasing.

examples.ko: 총리가 방한하면 두 나라 정상이 만날 거예요.
examples.en: When the prime minister visits Korea, the two countries' leaders will meet.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 영화 홍보를 위해 방한하지 않기로 했어요.
examples.en: The actor decided not to visit Korea to promote the film.

examples.ko: 교황이 방한할 때 많은 사람이 모일 거예요.
examples.en: Many people will gather when the Pope visits Korea.

explain: 외국 사람이 일이나 공식 일정으로 한국에 올 때 주로 써요. 한국 사람이 일본에 가면 '방일하다', 미국에 가면 '방미하다'처럼 나라 이름 한 글자를 붙여요. 그냥 놀러 온 친구 이야기에는 '한국에 오다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The president's schedule for visiting Korea was announced.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방한하다를 명사로 바꾼 말로, 외국 손님이 한국에 오는 계획을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun form of 방한하다, used for a foreign guest's plan to visit Korea.
phrases.en_equiv: schedule of a visit to Korea

phrases.example: 그 배우는 방한 중에 팬 미팅을 했어요.
phrases.en: The actor held a fan meeting while visiting Korea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외국 사람이 한국에 머무는 동안이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means while a foreign person is staying in Korea.

phrases.example: 제 친구가 다음 달에 한국에 와요.
phrases.en: My friend is coming to Korea next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 외국 친구가 한국에 올 때는 방한하다보다 이 말이 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily talk about a foreign friend coming to Korea, this sounds more natural than 방한하다.

explain_en: It is mainly used when a foreigner comes to Korea for work or an official schedule. When a Korean goes to Japan it is 방일하다, and to the US it is 방미하다, adding one syllable of the country name. For a friend who simply came to visit, 한국에 오다 sounds natural.

examples.ko: 물건의 수취 여부는 택배 조회 화면에서 바로 확인할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can check right away on the parcel tracking screen whether the item has been received.

examples.ko: 택배 송장에는 수취인 이름과 전화번호를 정확히 적어야 해요.
examples.en: On a parcel slip, you must write the recipient's name and phone number accurately.
You need an ID card to receive the mail in person.

examples.ko: 대금을 수취한 뒤에 영수증을 보내 드려요.
examples.en: I'll send you a receipt after I receive the payment.

examples.ko: 수취를 거부한 소포는 보낸 사람에게 다시 돌아가요.
examples.en: A parcel whose receipt was refused goes back to the sender.

examples.ko: 해외에서 보낸 돈을 수취하는 데 사흘쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes about three days to receive money sent from abroad.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '받다'라고 하고, '수취하다'는 택배, 우편, 대금처럼 서류나 안내문에서 많이 보여요. '수취인'의 반대는 '발송인'이에요.

phrases.en: I wrote the recipient's name wrong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이나 돈을 받는 사람을 뜻하며 택배 송장에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The person receiving an item or money, often seen on parcel slips.

phrases.en: You must receive the item yourself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류나 안내문에서 '물건을 받다'를 격식 있게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal way to say 'receive an item' in documents or notices.

phrases.en: I received a parcel yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '수취하다' 대신 '받다'를 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday speech, '받다' is used much more than '수취하다'.

explain_en: In everyday talk people simply say '받다'; '수취하다' shows up in documents and notices about parcels, mail and payments. The opposite of '수취인' (recipient) is '발송인' (sender).

examples.en: Can I go home now?
Now I get what you mean.
The rain has stopped, so shall we go out now?
Now I can do well even by myself.
I could not see it earlier, but I can see it now.
Stop fighting now and make up.

explain: '이제'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요. 말할 때 편하게 들리고, 글이나 발표에서는 '이제'가 더 일반적이에요.

phrases.en: Only now do I understand what you mean.
phrases.nuance_ko: '야'가 붙으면 한참 지나서 비로소 그렇게 되었다는 느낌이 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '야' stresses that something happened only after a long time.

phrases.en: From now on I'll study hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금부터 시작한다는 뜻이에요. 말할 때 편하게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means starting from this moment, and sounds casual in speech.

phrases.en: Can I go home now?
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이고 글이나 발표에서는 '이제'가 더 일반적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, and 이제 is the more standard choice in writing and presentations.

explain_en: It means the same as '이제' (now). It sounds relaxed in speech, while '이제' is the more general choice in writing and presentations.

p.n: Same meaning; 이제 is the standard form.

en: to warehouse; to store in warehouse; to stock

examples.en: We'll stock the new products in the warehouse tomorrow.
I took my car into the repair shop to get it fixed.
I'll let you know as soon as we get the new items in stock.
It's the day the bookstore takes in new books.

examples.ko: 물건을 입고할 때는 먼저 개수를 세어요.
examples.en: When taking in goods, we count the number first.
The store stocked its winter clothes yesterday.

explain: 반대말은 '출고하다'예요. '옷을 입고(입다)'와 소리가 같지만, 가게나 창고 이야기에서는 물건이 들어온다는 뜻이고 자동차를 정비소에 맡길 때도 써요. 물건이 주어면 '입고되다', 사람이 들여놓으면 '입고하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The new products arrived at the store yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 주어일 때는 피동 '입고되다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the passive 입고되다 when the goods are the subject.
phrases.en_equiv: to be stocked; to arrive in stock

phrases.example: 그 상품은 다음 주에 입고 예정이에요.
phrases.en: That item is scheduled to arrive next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쇼핑몰이나 가게에서 물건이 언제 들어오는지 말할 때 자주 봐요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen at shops and online stores when saying when goods will come in.

phrases.en: When is the arrival date?
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 창고나 가게에 들어오는 날을 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask the day goods come into the warehouse or shop.

explain_en: Its opposite is '출고하다' (ship out). It sounds the same as '옷을 입고' (wearing clothes), but in talk about shops and warehouses it means goods come in, and it is also used when you leave a car at a repair shop. With goods as the subject you say '입고되다', and with a person doing it, '입고하다'.

examples.en: The nurse took out a syringe.

examples.ko: 일회용 주사기는 한 번만 써야 해요.
examples.en: A disposable syringe must be used only once.
I get scared when I see a syringe needle.
I filled the syringe with the medicine little by little.

examples.ko: 실험실에서 물의 양을 재려고 주사기를 썼어요.
examples.en: In the lab, I used a syringe to measure the amount of water.

examples.ko: 아이는 주사기 모양 장난감을 가지고 놀아요.
examples.en: The child plays with a syringe-shaped toy.

explain: 몸에 약을 넣는 일은 '주사'이고, 그때 쓰는 도구는 '주사기'예요. '주사를 맞다'라고는 하지만 '주사기를 맞다'라고는 하지 않아요. 주사기는 '쓰다', '꽂다', '버리다' 같은 동사와 함께 써요.

phrases.en: The nurse put the medicine into the syringe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주사를 놓기 전에 주사기에 약을 채울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when filling a syringe with medicine before an injection.
phrases.en_equiv: to fill a syringe with medicine

phrases.en: You have to throw used syringes away separately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사용한 주사기는 일반 쓰레기와 다르게 버린다는 뜻으로 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is often said because used syringes are not thrown away with ordinary trash.

phrases.en: Hospitals always use a new syringe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번도 쓰지 않은 깨끗한 주사기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means a clean syringe that has never been used.

explain_en: Putting medicine into the body is 주사, and the tool used for it is 주사기. You say 주사를 맞다, but never 주사기를 맞다. 주사기 goes with verbs like 쓰다, 꽂다 and 버리다.
